lines.text: Programs need memory. Variables are how they remember scores, names, totals — anything that changes.
A variable is a named storage location.
Set gives it a value; change adds to it.
Its value can change while the program runs.
Ask and wait lets the user type.
Whatever they type is stored in answer.
Copy it into your own variable if you need it later.
Join sticks text together to build messages.
Name variables for what they hold: score, lives, total — not x1 or thing.
In Python, input is like ask and wait, and the variables a and b store the numbers.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
